name: 03 - HDR-Aware Transcode (HEVC/MP4, Preserves HDR Metadata)
description: HDR-safe variant of the full pipeline. Detects HDR (HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision) and routes appropriately: HDR files are stream-copied with container/audio/EAC3 fixes only. SDR files get full HEVC NVENC transcode with resolution-tiered quality and software fallback. Both paths support commentary removal, EAC3 5.1 surround, and Plex/arr notifications. Configure via the top variable nodes.

flowPlugins.name: Input File

── CONFIGURATION ─────────────────────────────
All user-configurable options are set here as
flow variables. Edit the VALUE field of each
'Set Variable' node below to configure:

  remove_commentary  (true/false)
    Remove director commentary, audio description,
    and hearing-impaired audio tracks.
    Default: true  ★ Opinionated — set false to keep.

  enable_plex_notify  (true/false)
    Trigger a Plex library refresh after each file
    is replaced. Requires Plex URL+token in the
    'Notify Plex' webRequest node near the bottom.
    Default: false  ★ Must configure URL+token first.

  enable_arr_notify  (true/false)
    Notify Radarr/Sonarr after file replacement.
    Requires API key in the 'Notify Arr' node.
    Default: false  ★ Must configure API key first.

Set Variable: remove_commentary
★ Change value to 'false' to keep commentary tracks

Set Variable: enable_plex_notify
★ Change value to 'true' to enable Plex refresh
   (also configure the webRequest node below)

Set Variable: enable_arr_notify
★ Change value to 'true' to enable Radarr/Sonarr notify
   (also configure the notifyRadarrOrSonarr node below)

── ABOUT THIS FLOW ───────────────────────────
HDR-AWARE variant of the Full Pipeline (Flow 01).

Problem this solves:
HDR video contains color metadata (HDR10 tone-
mapping curves, Dolby Vision RPU layers) that
MUST be preserved. Re-encoding strips this data,
causing washed-out colors or broken HDR display.

This flow's HDR strategy:
  HDR detected → STREAM COPY video only
    (MP4 container + audio fixed; no re-encode)
  SDR detected → Full HEVC NVENC transcode
    (same as Flow 01, with resolution-tiered QP)

Both paths:
  ✓ Remove commentary tracks (opt-in)
  ✓ Add EAC3 5.1 surround + stereo AAC 2.0
  ✓ Remove DTS + incompatible audio codecs
  ✓ Reorder streams (stereo AAC first)
  ✓ Validate output duration
  ✓ Optional Plex/arr notifications

★ IMPORTANT NOTES:
  • hvc1 tag and faststart work with stream copy
  • DV profile 5/8: stream copy is correct
  • DV profile 4/7 (dual-layer MKV): needs dovi_tool
    for full fidelity — stream copy still works but
    loses the enhancement layer
  • 10-bit SDR: follows the transcode path (correct)

── GUARD CHECKS ──────────────────────────────
Checks if the file is already fully optimal.
All 4 must pass to skip processing entirely.

  1. Container: MP4/M4V
  2. Video: HEVC codec
  3. Audio: Has AAC stream
  4. Audio: Has 2-channel stream

→ ALL PASS: mark as processed, no action
→ ANY FAIL: route through health check and
  HDR detection into the appropriate path

── HDR DETECTION ─────────────────────────────
Detects HDR content to route appropriately.

The checkHdr plugin checks for:
  • HDR10: SMPTE ST 2084 (PQ) transfer function
    + BT.2020 color primaries + TV color range
  • HLG: Hybrid Log-Gamma (arib-std-b67)
  • Dolby Vision: codec tags dvhe, dvav, dav1, dvh1

Outputs:
  → HDR DETECTED (1): stream-copy video path
  → SDR DETECTED (2): full NVENC transcode path

⚠ 10-BIT SDR NOTE:
  10-bit files that are NOT HDR (e.g., high-
  quality SDR masters) will follow the transcode
  path. NVENC handles 10-bit HEVC correctly.

Detect HDR Video
(checks HDR10, HLG, Dolby Vision metadata)

Outputs: YES=HDR (1) → stream-copy path
         NO=SDR  (2) → NVENC transcode path

── HDR PATH: VIDEO STREAM COPY ───────────────
HDR content detected. Stream-copying video to
preserve all HDR metadata perfectly.

This path:
  ✓ Sets container to MP4
  ✓ Removes subtitles (all)
  ✓ Removes data streams
  ✓ Removes commentary tracks (opt-in)
  ✓ Applies hvc1 tag + faststart
  ✓ Adds EAC3 5.1 surround (eng + und)
  ✓ Adds stereo AAC 2.0 (eng + und)
  ✓ Removes DTS + incompatible audio
  ✓ Reorders streams
  ✓ Validates output duration

It does NOT:
  ✗ Re-encode video (stream copy only)
  ✗ Validate file size (expected to change
    when remuxing MKV→MP4)

── SDR PATH: FULL HEVC NVENC TRANSCODE ───────
SDR content detected. Full transcode pipeline.

NVENC availability is checked first:
  NVENC available → resolution-tiered QP encoding
  NVENC unavailable → software libx265 fallback

Resolution-tiered quality (NVENC QP values):
  SD (≤720p)  → QP 26  (efficient for smaller res)
  1080p       → QP 24  (balanced quality/size)
  4K+         → QP 28  (efficient; 4K is very detailed)
  Unknown res → QP 24  (safe default)

★ CONFIGURE (click each encoder node):
  - ffmpegQuality: QP value (20=high, 28=efficient)
  - ffmpegPreset: slow (maps to NVENC p6)
  - forceEncoding: false (stream-copies HEVC)
  - SW fallback: ffmpegQuality=22 (libx265 CRF)

Size limit: output rejected if >120% of source.

── NVENC AVAILABILITY CHECK (SDR) ────────────
Checks if the NVENC GPU encoder is available
on this Tdarr worker node.

Outputs:
  YES (1) → NVENC available → resolution-tiered encode
  NO  (2) → NVENC unavailable → software libx265

This prevents hard failures when:
  • The T400 GPU session limit (4) is reached
  • Running on a CPU-only worker node
  • GPU driver/runtime not accessible

Check: NVENC Encoder Available?
(hevc_nvenc on this worker node)

Outputs: YES → Resolution tiers | NO → SW fallback

── RESOLUTION-TIERED QUALITY (SDR) ───────────
Routes to different QP values based on resolution.

Outputs from checkVideoResolution:
  1=480p  → SD encoder (QP 26)
  2=576p  → SD encoder (QP 26)
  3=720p  → SD encoder (QP 26)
  4=1080p → 1080p encoder (QP 24)
  5=1440p → 4K encoder (QP 28)
  6=4K    → 4K encoder (QP 28)
  7=DCI4K → 4K encoder (QP 28)
  8=8K    → 4K encoder (QP 28)
  9=Other → 1080p encoder (QP 24, safe default)

★ Configure QP in each encoder node below.

Check Video Resolution
(routes to appropriate quality tier)

Set Video Encoder → HEVC NVENC (SD: ≤720p)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=26 | ffmpegPreset=slow
  forceEncoding=false (stream-copies existing HEVC)

Set Video Encoder → HEVC NVENC (1080p / Unknown)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=24 | ffmpegPreset=slow
  forceEncoding=false (stream-copies existing HEVC)

Set Video Encoder → HEVC NVENC (4K+)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=28 | ffmpegPreset=slow
  forceEncoding=false (stream-copies existing HEVC)

── SOFTWARE FALLBACK ENCODER (SDR) ───────────
NVENC is NOT available on this worker.
Falling back to libx265 software encoding.

libx265 uses CRF (Constant Rate Factor):
  CRF 22 = visually near-lossless quality
  CRF 28 = efficient, slight quality reduction

Software encoding is much slower than NVENC
but produces the same output format.

★ Config: ffmpegQuality=22 (CRF 22)

Set Video Encoder → HEVC Software (libx265)
★ Config: ffmpegQuality=22 (CRF) | ffmpegPreset=slow
